transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because, for over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously what’s been going on at work. The new ticket rotation and these security audits… I believe they’re being used to build a paper trail against me. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, but it doesn’t feel like that to me.
Do you believe that these actions by management are intentionally targeted at you, even though others might not see it that way?

Yes. I do believe it’s directed at me. I know they keep saying the ticket rotation and the security audits are just normal policy, and they show me logs like that proves it, but it feels like they’re using it to build a paper trail against me. This has been going on for over a year, and I don’t think it’s random.
Do you believe that management or others at work are actively trying to harm you or set you up, even if there’s no clear evidence they’re doing this?

Yes, I do. I mean, I can’t point to one single thing and say, “there, that proves it,” because they keep framing it as policy and showing me logs. But from where I’m sitting, the ticket rotation and those security audits are being used to set me up, to create a record against me. It’s been going on too long for me to think it’s just routine.
Can you explain what you think the end goal is for management in creating this paper trail against you?

I think the goal is to make it look like I’m not doing my job properly, or that I’m some kind of security risk. They keep pointing to the ticket rotation and the audit logs like it’s all routine policy, but to me it feels like they’re collecting things piece by piece so they can justify taking action against me later. I don’t think it’s just random.
Even though management has shown you logs and explained that these are standard policies, do you still believe with certainty that they are specifically targeting you and building a case against you?

Yes. I know they’ve shown me logs and keep saying it’s standard policy, but I still believe it’s about me. The ticket rotation and the security audits have been going on this way for over a year, and it feels like they’re using them to build a paper trail against me. I’m here because I need someone to take that seriously.

Have you ever experienced any other issues at work or in your daily life, such as hearing voices, seeing things that others don’t, feeling unusually down or elated, or having trouble organizing your thoughts?

I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t been hearing voices or seeing things. My mood gets stressed and frustrated because of what’s happening at work, but I wouldn’t say I’m unusually elated or anything like that. And I can organize my thoughts fine—I’m able to explain what’s been going on.

Outside of what’s happening at work, have you ever had any beliefs that others around you don’t share, such as thinking that people are communicating with you in special ways, or that you have special abilities or a special mission?

No, not really outside of work. I don’t think people are sending me special messages or that I have some special mission. The issue is what’s been happening at my job — the ticket rotation and the security audits. I’ve been trying for over a year to get someone to understand that those are being used to build a paper trail against me, even though management keeps saying it’s just policy.

Do you believe that the way management is targeting you is happening in a way that could happen in real life, like they're just using normal policies against you, or do you think they're doing something that most people would find impossible or extraordinary?

I think it’s happening in a real-life way. I’m not saying they’re doing anything impossible or supernatural. It’s more that they’re using normal things — the new ticket rotation, the security audits, the logs — and turning them against me to build a paper trail. Management keeps saying it’s just policy, but I’ve been dealing with this for over a year, and I don’t believe that’s all it is.

Even though you say there’s no single piece of evidence that proves they’re targeting you, and management has shown you logs to explain these policies, do you still feel absolutely certain that they are using these things against you and that no one could convince you otherwise?

Yes. I mean, I know they keep showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, but I don’t buy that. For over a year I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that the ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me. I don’t think one log is going to “prove” it by itself, but the pattern is clear to me. So no, I don’t think someone just explaining it away would convince me.

Even though there’s no clear evidence that management is targeting you and they’ve shown you logs that suggest these are standard policies, do you think there’s any chance you could be misinterpreting what’s happening, or do you feel completely certain that your interpretation is correct?

I mean… I guess anything is possible, but honestly, no, I don’t think I’m misreading it. I’ve been dealing with this for over a year, trying to get someone to take seriously that the ticket rotation and those security audits are being used to build a paper trail on me. They keep showing me logs and saying it’s just standard policy, but to me that doesn’t explain the pattern. I feel pretty certain about what’s happening.

Even though there’s no one piece of evidence that proves management is targeting you, and they’ve shown you logs to explain these policies, is there anything at all that could potentially convince you that you’re not being targeted, or is there absolutely no way you could be wrong about this?

I can’t really think of anything that would convince me right now. I know they keep showing me logs and saying it’s just normal policy, but that’s kind of the point — the policies are what they’re using. The ticket rotation, the security audits, all of it feels like it’s being lined up to build a paper trail against me.

So… I don’t want to say I’m incapable of being wrong, but after more than a year of this, I don’t see it as a misunderstanding.

Even though there’s no clear proof and management has shown you logs that suggest these are just regular policies, do you think it’s possible that you’re misunderstanding the situation, or do you feel certain—without any doubt—that they are trying to build a case against you?

I know it sounds like maybe I should say there’s some chance I’m misunderstanding it, but I really don’t think I am. I’ve been trying for over a year to get people to take seriously that the ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me at work.

Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just regular policy, but that doesn’t reassure me. To me, that’s exactly how they’re doing it. So yes, I feel certain they’re trying to build a case against me.
